memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When two full years had passed, Pharaoh had a dream: He was standing by the Nile, when out of the river there came up seven cows, sleek and fat, and they grazed among the reeds. After them, seven other cows, ugly and gaunt, came up out of the Nile and stood beside those on the riverbank. And the cows that were ugly and gaunt ate up the seven sleek, fat cows. Then Pharaoh woke up. He fell asleep again and had a second dream: Seven heads of grain, healthy and good, were growing on a single stalk. After them, seven other heads of grain sprouted—thin and scorched by the east wind. The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven healthy, full heads. Then Pharaoh woke up; it had been a dream." - Gen 41:1-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two full years after Joseph had asked the cupbearer to remember him, God finally moves — not through the cupbearer, but through Pharaoh himself. The king has two strange, disturbing dreams: seven fat cows swallowed by seven gaunt ones, and seven healthy heads of grain devoured by seven withered ones. Pharaoh wakes troubled, sensing these dreams mean something he cannot grasp.

Notice first the timing: "when two full years had passed." God's clock is not ours. Joseph had waited and waited, seemingly forgotten. But God was not idle; He was waiting for the precise moment. When the time was exactly right, He set events in motion through the dreams of a pagan king.

Notice also who is dreaming. God speaks to Pharaoh, a man who did not know or worship Him. This shows that God is sovereign over all people and all nations, even those far from Him. The most powerful ruler on earth is a small figure in God's hands, used to accomplish God's purposes.

If you are in a long season of waiting, remember these "two full years." God has not forgotten you, and He is not late. He is working out His plan through people and events you cannot see, waiting for the right moment. The God who moves the heart of kings is at work in your story too, and His timing, though it stretches our patience, is always perfect.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I trusting God's timing even in a long season of waiting?
2. Do I believe God is sovereign over even the powerful and the faraway?
3. Where do I need to remember that God is not idle or late?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I must wait, remind me that You are never idle and never late. You move the hearts of kings and work out Your plan in perfect timing. Help me to trust You while I wait. Amen.
